subject: Post-call: ACME integration — model routing & policy configuration

Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - ACME integration (model routing + policies)

Alex / Priya - thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Summary (what we discussed)
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood inference for ACME's customer support assistant (real-time chat + batch reranks for search).
- Key success metrics: median p99 latency target <= 350ms on chat flows, cost target $0.0008 / token equivalent for high-volume flows, embedding recall >= 92% at current eval sets.
- Integration scope: SDK setup and auth, model routing & policy config (latency/cost/fallback chains), structured output/tool calling for ticket triage, embeddings + reranker for semantic search.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) We'll send our integration guide and a scoping worksheet (attached) - please fill environment details and peak qps.
2) Schedule an architecture workshop with our SE (Dev) to walk through SDK auth, routing policies, and a draft config. Suggested 60-90 min.
3) Confirm any hard constraints (SLA/region/data residency) - I noted you want US multiregional routing and SOC2 evidence; if there are other controls let us know.

Notes for architecture workshop (high-level)
- SDK and auth: short-lived API keys or mTLS depending on ACME environment; we'll show example client config and token rotation.
- Model routing: route by intent/latency requirements - e.g., low-latency chat -> quantized local variant; high-quality long-form -> higher-cost model. Fallback chains and region affinity to keep p99 bounded.
- Structured output / tool calling: we support function-calling-style structured JSON outputs and can plug in ticketing webhooks.
- Embeddings / reranker: recommend a two-stage flow (embedding retrieval -> light reranker model) to balance cost/quality.

Attachments: redwood-integration-guide.pdf, acme-scoping-sheet.xlsx

Thanks - I'll coordinate times for the workshop once I hear availability.

- Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - ACME integration (model routing + policies)

Hi Alex / Priya - quick technical notes ahead of the workshop. I'll walk through these live but want to share an initial blueprint so you can surface any constraints early.

1) SDK setup & auth - SDKs: we provide Java, Python, and Node clients. Basic flow: instantiate client with API key OR configure mTLS client cert. Example client config (pseudo):
  - api_key: <short-lived token from KMS>
  - region: us-east-1
  - prefer_low_latency: true
  - default_model: rwd-chat-lite-v1
- Auth: API keys are easiest; for stricter security we support mutual TLS and integration with enterprise KMS (you can rotate keys via our console or API).

2) Model routing & policy configuration (examples) - Policy layers we typically use:
  a) Route by route/intent: e.g., "support_chat" -> low-latency variant, "draft_summary" -> quality variant.
  b) Cost/latency tiering: define tiers (fast/standard/quality) with explicit model bundles and max_latency thresholds.
  c) Fallback chains: primary -> secondary quantized -> remote fallback; each has a max token limit and cumulative timeout.

Example policy (pseudo-DSL):
  route "support_chat" {
    tiers: [fast, standard]
    fast { model: rwd-chat-lite-8q, max_latency_ms: 200, cost_limit_usd: 0.0006 }
    standard { model: rwd-chat-xl, max_latency_ms: 500, cost_limit_usd: 0.0012 }
    fallback: [fast -> standard -> remote-high-quality]
    region_affinity: [us-east-1, us-west-2]
  }

Notes on region routing / KV cache:
- We recommend region_affinity so requests prefer a nearby region and only failover on capacity or health events.
- KV cache (prefix + attention cache) is per-region; cross-region hits are possible but add ~30-60ms depending on link and size. For p99-sensitive flows, keep affinity to a single region and use warm-up batching.

3) Structured output / tool-calling - We support function-calling style JSON outputs and can enforce schemas. For ticket triage we can map fields directly to your ticketing API (webhook) or produce a structured payload to be validated client-side.

4) Embeddings & reranker - Two-stage retrieval recommended: embeddings for candidate retrieval -> cheap reranker (small decoder or cross-encoder) for precision.
- You can continue using Pinecone; we integrate via standard vector API. Benefits of our managed vector store: tighter caching, co-located embeddings near inference region, and simpler end-to-end tracing.

Attachments / links:
- Quickstart SDK bundle: redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip (attached to this thread)
- Integration docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-integration

I'll prepare a draft routing policy and share before the workshop. Proposed workshop agenda: 1) confirm auth & network, 2) live SDK quickstart, 3) routing policy walkthrough + Q&A, 4) embeddings/re-ranker discussion.

- Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
